title: Smooth base change for limits of smooth schemes
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and let $I$ be a nonempty directed set. Let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of schemes over $S$, with structure maps $g_i:S_i\to S$ which are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Suppose $S'=\varprojlim_i S_i$, with induced structure map $g:S'\to S$. Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and form the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'=X\times_S S'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
S'&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Let $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ be a bounded below complex of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume its cohomology has torsion orders invertible on $S$: explicitly, for every integer $q$, every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, and every element $v\in\mathcal H^q(E)_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], there is a positive integer $n$ such that $nv=0$ and $n\cdot1$ is a unit in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. No common annihilator is required. Then the canonical bounded below derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]
$$
\Ex_{\square,E}:g^{-1}Rf_*E\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}E
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(S'_{\Et})$. Here $u^{-1}$ and $Ru_*$ are inverse image and derived direct image of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This is Stacks Tag 0F09 in the case in which the maps $S_i\to S$ are also quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: Transport each algebraically closed geometric-stalk annihilator in hE to a separably closed geometric stalk by precomposing its point with Spec of its algebraic closure. Scheme.isIso_pointSmallEtalePrecomp_sheafFiber is a proved additive isomorphism, so injectivity transports n*x=0 back to the original stalk, retaining the same positive integer and global unit.

proof.text: For an abelian sheaf F with this elementwise condition, use the existing equivalence sheafCompose(forget from ULift Z modules) to choose its uniquely determined module encoding G and its comparison eF. The proved Point.sheafFiberCompIso and eF identify the underlying module stalk with the abelian stalk. Its injective additive comparison transfers annihilators, giving Scheme.IsTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder S G. Apply the recorded smooth base change theorem, via the already proved isIso_baseChange_app_singleFunctor_obj_of_smooth of SmoothBaseChange/Derived.lean, to each stage. The source-library DerivedForget theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_app_forget₂_iff and the exact functor single comparison transport the same canonical exchange back to F. This uses no choice from an unproved mere existence theorem: objPreimage and objObjPreimageIso belong to the proved equivalence.

proof.text: Construct the pointwise fibre products X ×_S D_i, their two projection natural transformations and the cone from X-prime using pullback.lift. Prove the cone is limiting directly: any competing cone gives a map to X by the constant-cone universal property and a map to c.pt by hc; their composites to S agree at any chosen index. The chosen pullback square lifts them uniquely to X-prime. Checking both projections proves factorization and uniqueness. MorphismProperty.pullbackMap gives affine transitions from htrans; constant diagrams have identity transitions. No absolute quasi-compactness assumption on S is used.

proof.text: Apply higherDirectImage_baseChange_of_limit to the four diagrams (D, pulled-back D, constant S, constant X), with direct-image leg the constant f. Its finite-stage hypotheses are Step 2. Its coefficient sheaves are all F, with transition maps upperStarId.hom. The upperStarComp unit laws prove their identity and composition conditions and the compatibility with the constant diagram with value F. The latter has cocone F and is colimiting since I is connected; the two constant scheme cones are likewise limiting. Positive elementwise annihilators give Sheaf.IsTorsion F. The conclusion proves invertibility of each nonnegative cohomology map of the canonical exchange on F[0]. In negative degrees both sides are zero: right derived direct image preserves the lower bound zero and exact inverse image preserves cohomology. DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_iff therefore makes exchange on F[0] invertible.

proof.text: Apply the already proved source-library tool DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_app_of_forall_homology (WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.PlusDevissage) to the canonical exchange and the object property P(F) = exchange on F[0] is invertible. Naturality makes P invariant under isomorphisms. The triangulated and shift-compatible structures of canonical exchange are existing ones. Both composite functors preserve every lower cohomology bound: apply right-derived negative vanishing and the exact-inverse-image homology comparison, in the source and target orders respectively. Step 4 and Step 1 give P(H^q(E)) for every q. The tool performs finite induction along truncation triangles and the bounded-below truncation comparison, proving precisely the asserted exchange isomorphism. Thus no explicit exact couples, convergence data or finite-filtration induction are needed; no realized statement or proof step of the containing unit is bypassed (its realized fields are empty).

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $S'=\varprojlim_iS_i$ a directed inverse
limit of schemes $S_i$ which are
smooth, quasi-compact and
quasi-separated over $S$, with affine transition morphisms. Let
$f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact
and quasi-separated and form the
cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{\;g'\;}&X\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
S'&\xrightarrow{\;g\;}&S .
\end{array}
$$

Then $g^{-1}Rf_*E=Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E$ for any
$E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ whose cohomology sheaves have stalks which are
torsion of orders invertible on $S$, in the sense of
[def-kun-torsion-invertible].

proof.text:
*Step 1 (the sheaf case).* Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on
$X_{\Et}$ with torsion stalks of orders invertible on $S$, and fix
$p\ge0$. For every $i$ form the cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;g'_i\;}&X\times_SS_i\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f_i}\\
S&\xleftarrow{\;g_i\;}&S_i
\end{array}
$$

with $g_i:S_i\to S$ smooth and quasi-compact and quasi-separated
([def-sbc-smooth-morphisms],
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) and
$f_i=f\times_S\id_{S_i}$. The schemes $X\times_SS_i$ form an inverse
system with affine transition morphisms whose limit is
$X'=X\times_SS'$, by
[lem-kun-fibre-product-limits] (limits and fibre products commute), so
the squares displayed above form an inverse system of cartesian squares, in
the sense of [lem-kun-0ezt], with limit the square of the
statement.

Since $g_i$ is smooth and $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the
smooth base change theorem [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] of the smooth-base-change chapter,
applied to the displayed square in the transposed orientation, gives

$$
g_i^{-1}R^pf_*F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R^pf_{i,*}(g'_i)^{-1}F ,
$$

the coefficient $F$ having torsion stalks of orders invertible on $S$,
hence on the smooth $S$-scheme $S_i$. The sheaves
$F_i:=(g'_i)^{-1}F$ form a compatible system with
$\varinjlim_ip_i^{-1}F_i=(g')^{-1}F$, so the higher-direct-image form
[lem-kun-0ezt] of the limit statement, applied for the fixed $p$,
yields

$$
g^{-1}R^pf_*F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R^pf'_*(g')^{-1}F .
$$

*Step 2 (the complex case).* Let $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ be as in the
statement. By [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] the two
hypercohomology spectral sequences

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(E)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*E),
\qquad
E_2'^{p,q}=R^pf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal H^q(E)
\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E)
$$

are defined by the truncation filtrations, and by
[lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence] the induced filtrations in
each degree are finite, exhaustive and separated. The exchange morphism
$g^{-1}Rf_*E\to Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is
natural in the coefficient object
([lem-kun-bc-base-change]), so it is compatible with the truncation
triangles and induces a morphism of filtered objects, hence a morphism of
the two spectral sequences which on $E_2^{p,q}$ is the base-change map
$g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(E)\to R^pf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal H^q(E)$. By Step
1 this is an isomorphism for every $(p,q)$; a morphism of spectral
sequences which is an isomorphism on $E_2$ is an isomorphism on every
$E_r$ and hence on the associated graded objects of the abutments. Since
the filtrations are finite, [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction]
upgrades this to an isomorphism of the abutments in every degree, i.e. to

$$
\mathcal H^n\bigl(g^{-1}Rf_*E\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\mathcal H^n\bigl(Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E\bigr)\qquad(n\in\mathbf Z).
$$

A morphism in $D(S'_{\Et})$ which is an isomorphism on all cohomology
sheaves is an isomorphism ([def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]), which is
the assertion.
